cards.front: When is $AB$ defined, and what is its shape?
cards.back: When the number of columns of $A$ equals the number of rows of $B$. If $A$ is $m \times n$ and $B$ is $n \times p$, then $AB$ is $m \times p$.

cards.front: Column $j$ of $AB$ is a combination of which vectors, and what are the weights?
cards.back: It combines the columns of $A$, with the entries of column $j$ of $B$ as weights.

cards.front: What does a column times a row give, and how do such products build $AB$?
cards.back: A full matrix whose columns are multiples of the column and whose rows are multiples of the row. $AB$ is the sum over $k$ of column $k$ of $A$ times row $k$ of $B$.

cards.front: Which law always holds for matrix products, and which one can fail?
cards.back: $(AB)C = A(BC)$ always holds. $AB = BA$ can fail.

cards.front: Why does a square matrix $A$ with $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$ for some nonzero $\mathbf{x}$ have no inverse?
cards.back: An inverse would give $\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}A\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\mathbf{0} = \mathbf{0}$.

cards.front: In Gauss–Jordan elimination, what do you start from and where do you read $A^{-1}$?
cards.back: Start from $\begin{bmatrix} A & I \end{bmatrix}$ and eliminate until the left half is $I$. The right half is then $A^{-1}$.
